demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Memory.value: I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind.
When I remember the event I feel intense rage
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning

Negative Appraisals.value: Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore
I acted in ways that go against who I am
The event happened because of the way I acted

issues.item: Memory Feels Alien: The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me
issues.explanation: The trauma type is accidentally causing serious injury to another person. 'Memory Feels Alien' can occur in PTSD, but paired with the available appraisal pattern it suggests stronger dissociation/self-detachment than is otherwise represented; more importantly, the memory cluster centers on fragmented visual recall and rage, whereas the appraisal cluster centers on guilt/meaning plus personal bodily damage, making the profile feel pulled between different trauma experiences.

issues.item: Physical Vulnerability: My body has been permanently damaged by what happened
issues.explanation: 'Physical Vulnerability: My body has been permanently damaged by what happened' is hard to reconcile with the indexed trauma type, which is causing serious injury to another person rather than being physically injured oneself. Unless the event also seriously injured the patient, this item is clinically implausible. It also does not fit well with the Memory → Negative Appraisals formulation, because the memory items provided more naturally support guilt, shame, or moral injury appraisals such as 'Violated Values' rather than permanent bodily damage.

vignette: Suresh, a 52-year-old South Asian man and former maid, has been grappling with profound distress since an accident at work led to serious injury for one of his colleagues. The event remains etched in Suresh's mind as disjointed snapshots, each a vivid picture that captures the horror and helplessness he experienced. One moment is particularly searing: the sound of metal scraping against concrete just before the impact that sent his coworker tumbling into an open elevator shaft. Each time these images resurface, they trigger intense feelings of rage within Suresh. The sudden and unexpected nature of these memories can be jarring, often leaving him shaken in the middle of his daily tasks. While working in a busy hotel kitchen, the clatter of pots and pans might instantly transport him back to that fateful day. He has come to dread such moments because they invariably lead to a deep sense of self-blame. Suresh's feelings of intense self-blame have left him questioning every aspect of his life's meaning. The event happened because he acted in ways that, in retrospect, felt like an affront to who he truly is-a careful and conscientious person. This discrepancy has led to a pervasive sense of guilt and shame, eroding the value he once placed on his work and relationships. He had come to believe that nothing in his life feels meaningful anymore. His divorce further compounds these feelings, as Suresh's wife left him shortly after the incident. She couldn't bear to see him so consumed by self-reproach and unable to find any joy or purpose in their daily lives together. The weight of this loss has deepened his sense of isolation and despair. Suresh's negative appraisals are intricately tied to the intrusive memories he experiences. Each vivid flashback serves as a relentless reminder of his perceived failures, reinforcing his belief that he violated his own values and acted in ways antithetical to who he is. This loop has tightened over time, leaving him feeling increasingly trapped by these thoughts. What frightens Suresh most is the fear that this guilt will consume him entirely, preventing any chance at redemption or peace. His current state leaves him questioning if there's a way back from this abyss of self-loathing and regret. The cumulative toll on his mental health and relationships has finally brought him to seek help, hoping for some respite from the unrelenting cycle of memory and self-blame that haunts him. Suresh is most hopeful for finding a way to reconcile his past actions with who he wants to be moving forward. He seeks support in understanding how to regain meaning and purpose in his life, and ultimately find a path towards healing.
